items.title: Kandinsky 6.0 Video: Foundation Models for Synchronized Video and Audio Generation
items.summary: We present Kandinsky 6.0 Video, a family of foundation diffusion models for synchronized text-to-audio-video generation, comprising Kandinsky 6.0 Video Lite (3B parameters) and Kandinsky 6.0 Video Pro (29B parameters). items.title: ALoDLM: Adaptively Looped Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) enable fast generation by predicting multiple tokens in parallel, but their practical adoption remains limited by a persistent quality gap relative to comparably sized autoregressive (AR) models. items.title: Memadapter: Counterfactual Adaptation Against Memory-induced Sycophancy
items.summary: Long-term memory enables LLM-based agents to retain and reuse information across tasks and sessions, supporting personalization and long-horizon interactions. items.title: In-Distribution Forcing for Long Video Generation at Test Time
items.summary: Modern autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models excel at short-horizon video generation, yet generating long videos remains challenging due to drifting, where colors and textures shift, and motion dynamics decay. items.title: Foundations of Proactive Agents: Principles, Technical Layers, and Proactivity-Gym
items.summary: Proactive LLM agents can turn idle compute into useful support before users ask. Yet even correct work can misread user context, impose review costs, or undermine trust. items.title: Optimizing the Optimizer: Language Models Discover Faster Molecular Relaxation
items.summary: Geometry optimization is a major cost in many quantum-chemical workflows: each optimization step requires one force evaluation, and at the density-functional level that evaluation dominates the wall time. items.title: Self-Generated Feedback Destabilizes Test-Time Training: A Causal Decomposition of Long-Horizon Adaptation
items.summary: Test-time training (TTT) lets a model store information in its weights during inference. items.summary: Multimodal RAG retrieves text, tables, images, and videos, but choosing a retrieval granularity does not determine how much context to retain within each item. items.title: ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience
items.summary: A large language model (LLM) agent solves long-horizon tasks through many reasoning-action turns, with one verification signal at termination. items.title: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Evaluation of Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) is often limited to the final deliverables they create (at the end of hundreds of steps) and assessed with functional verifiers, as seen in OSWorld. items.title: OmniReasoning: Pushing the Limits of Audio-Visual Joint Reasoning
items.summary: Recent advances have enabled unified omni-modal models in understanding audio, vision, and language. However, existing benchmarks, training data, and learning methods largely treat the modalities independently, leaving the capability of audio-visual joint reasoning poorly evaluated and insufficiently elicited. items.title: Data Unlearning via Inverse Distillation
items.summary: Multi-step matching models, including flow and diffusion models, produce high-quality outputs but incur substantial inference costs and may reproduce unwanted components of their training datasets. We introduce Inverse Distillation Unlearning (IDU), a unified framework that simultaneously distills a teacher multi-step matching model into an efficient one-step student generator and suppresses outputs corresponding to a designated training subset.

items.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
items.summary: Every recurrence of a looped language model adds cost in training, decoding, prefill, and reinforcement learning (RL). The closer recurrent states get to fixed points, the less the path to them matters. items.title: SearchJev: A Fast and Calibrated System-1 Model for Search Agents
items.summary: Search agents repeatedly make short decisions about relevance, evidence sufficiency, and search actions. Using generative language models for these decisions introduces latency and unreliable confidence. We present SearchJev, a fast and calibrated System-1 model that separates search decisions from System-2 reasoning and generation. items.title: RobotUse: Allocating Computation, Context, and Decisions
items.summary: Robot agents must connect their intended actions to observed outcomes while retaining the context needed to revise their choices over repeated attempts. Existing interfaces often leave these choices inside predefined tools or require agents to manage detailed execution code and its growing history. items.title: Certification of Real Images through Calibrated Content Authentication
items.summary: Generative models can synthesize high-quality inauthentic multimedia content that is already being misused at scale. We evaluate twenty deepfake detectors against ten generators released in the last four years and find accuracy decreasing over time, from near-perfect 99.5% to 76%. items.title: Noise Out, Bias In: Targeted Bias Injection in Diffusion Language Models via Closed-Loop Activation Steering
items.summary: Masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising masked positions, re-predicting each token multiple times before it is committed. items.title: When to Switch: Reliable Action-Chunk Extension for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models serve as unified policies for robotic manipulation, yet their expensive inference forces robots to pause between policy calls, resulting in stop-and-go execution that interrupts smooth motion and prolongs task completion. items.title: RealtimeWAM: One-Step Asynchronous World Action Models
items.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) incorporate visual representations from video generation backbones to guide action prediction. Recent efficient WAMs adopt Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architectures and compute video representations once for reuse by the action expert. However, intra-expert iteration (\ie, multi-step action denoising) and inter-expert waiting (\ie, sequential execution of the video and action experts) still limit inference efficiency.

items.summary: A vision--language--action (VLA) policy can complete complex tasks while ignoring the evidence that should determine its actions. An object held near the wrist camera can displace the instructed target. items.title: QuantCode Model: Specializing Language Models for Executable Algorithmic Trading Code
items.summary: Large language models are strong general-purpose code generators, but executable algorithmic trading remains a demanding specialization target: a model must translate a natural-language strategy specification into correct program logic for a specialized trading framework, execute on historical data, produce trades, and remain semantically faithful to the request. items.title: Dynamic Harness Search: Building Multi-Agent Systems Per-Query via Prediction
items.summary: Agent harnesses specify the roles, instructions, tools, and communication structure used to solve a task, and the right harness depends on the query. items.title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
items.summary: Tool-using AI agents are increasingly deployed across enterprise software systems, yet widely used benchmarks primarily evaluate nominal task completion, conflating baseline planning competence with operational fault recovery. items.summary: We introduce a post-training method for diffusion language models (DLMs) that minimizes Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) between generated and reference distributions in the feature space of a frozen pretrained DLM.
